newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends firm as consolidation counters data.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends firm as consolidation counters data.

text.p: IPE Brent crude ended firm but off session highs on Thursday as dealers continued to opt for consolidation after a dramatic slide earlier this week.
Mildly bearish U.S. inventory data pushed prompt Brent to a low of $19.10 before a wave of short-covering and technical strength lifted the contract to $19.63, the high for the day.
July Brent ended 25 cents firmer at $19.49 as dealers still nervous after Tuesday's 78-cent slide, took profits.
"The normal scenario following a steep drop such as we have seen is for more than one day of consolidation," said Charles Gray of brokers Prudential Bache.

U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) data released on Thursday showed crude stocks rose by 3.2 million barrels last week. A rise of 1.1 million barrels in gasoline stocks was enough to provoke a mild sell-off in early NYMEX dealing.
Support held and a break back above $21.00 a barrel on July NYMEX crude gave the reversal an early technical boost.
"The break through $21.00 (a barrel) triggered a few buy-stops," said a broker.
July Brent's break above Wednesday's high of $19.34 and through resistance at $19.43 generated further momentum of its own but a stiffer barrier at $19.63 held firm, dealers said.
Earlier, IPE gas oil closed firmer, pulled nearly $3 off session lows by Brent's rally and firmer heating oil markets in the U.S.
June gas oil closed at $174.50 a tonne, up $1.25 on Wednesday's close and $2.75 above the intraday low. But the prompt contract continued to lag July, which gained $2.00 to $175.00.
Dealers said the wider contango suggested softer sentiment on European spot markets where trade was subdued by a holiday in much of Germany, Europe's biggest gas oil importer.
